subject: Re: Non-training assurance — telemetry & retention carve-outs
messages:
From: Liam Torres <liam.torres@acmehealth.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.ai>
Cc: security@acmehealth.com
Date: 2028-06-25 09:12 PDT
Subject: Clarify: 'we do not train on customer data' — telemetry edge cases

Hi Mina,

Quick question from our security review: your security slide deck says Redwood does not use customer request payloads to train models. We appreciate that. Two follow-ups from our auditors: (1) Does that non-training guarantee include short-lived telemetry (e.g., GPU perf traces, kernel crash dumps) that might incidentally contain snippets of request text? (2) For logs/backups/snapshots retained for incident debugging, are those ever used to update model weights via internal research experiments?

We need simple, categorical answers and any relevant retention SLAs so we can close this item with procurement.

Thanks — Liam
Liam Torres
Security Engineer, Acme Health

From: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.ai>
To: Liam Torres <liam.torres@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-06-25 10:05 PDT
Subject: Re: Clarify: 'we do not train on customer data' — telemetry edge cases

Liam — thanks for the clear asks. Short answers up front: (A) No, short-lived telemetry and kernel traces are NOT used to train our production or research models. (B) Logs/backups/snapshots retained for debugging are not routed into model training pipelines.

Details below and attaching a short FAQ and retention matrix that explain the limited exceptions and where telemetry is stored/for how long. Key points:
- Telemetry containing request payloads is sanitized and stored in an encrypted telemetry cluster with a maximum retention of 30 days by default for hosted customers.
- Customers on Dedicated/Private can opt into shorter retention or disable telemetry forwarding entirely (via Console > Diagnostics).
- Operational snapshots (for incident replay) are retained per customer-configured snapshot TTL; by default snapshot archives are kept 90 days but marked "operational only" and access is logged.
- There is a firm policy prohibiting adding any customer data source to model training datasets unless explicit written approval is given by our Legal + Research leads, and the data is subject to an additional review and anonymization pipeline.

I'll loop in Legal (Neha) and Platform Ops (Grace) to provide the formal language you can attach to your procurement docs.

—Mina
Mina Haddad
Director, Sales Engineering
Redwood Inference

-----BEGIN FORWARDED MESSAGE-----
From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-06-25 13:15 PDT
To: security@acmehealth.com
Subject: Redwood Data Use & Training Assurance (formal)

Acme Security Team,

Per your request, Redwood Inference provides the following assurances regarding customer data and model training: 

1) No-Training Guarantee: Redwood does not use customer request payloads, customer-uploaded documents, or customer-managed private data stores to train or update any production or research LLM weights by default. 

2) Telemetry and Operational Artifacts: Telemetry (performance traces, kernel logs, crash dumps) and operational snapshots may temporarily contain fragments of customer inputs. Such artifacts are:
   - Isolated to encrypted operational systems;
   - Retained only for a bounded period (default 30 days for telemetry; default 90 days for snapshots) unless otherwise configured by the customer;
   - Access is restricted to a small set of SRE/Platform engineers and is audited.

3) Prohibition on Training Use: Operational artifacts are explicitly excluded from any automated training ingestion pipelines. Any request to use such artifacts for research or model improvement requires: written approval from the customer (for customer data), sign-off from Redwood Legal, and a documented anonymization and risk review.

4) Customer Controls: Customers on Dedicated or Private deployments can further constrain retention, disable telemetry collection, or route telemetry to customer-managed storage.

If you need a standalone letter (PDF) on company letterhead, we can generate one once procurement confirms the wording.

Regards,
Neha Kapoor
Head of Legal — Redwood Inference
-----END FORWARDED MESSAGE-----

From: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>

Date: 2028-06-26 09:46 PDT
Subject: Re: Telemetry & retention carve-outs (operational note)

Adding operational specifics for Acme's security team: 

- Telemetry pipeline: traces and kernel logs are ingested into a restricted diagnostics cluster (EBS encrypted at rest, TLS in transit). Only a scoped SRE role can access the raw traces; everything else is surfaced via aggregated dashboards.
- Sanitization: request text is redacted by default from traces; we retain the ingress/egress token counts and timing metrics. In rare cases (crash analysis) a team member may request a blurred snippet to debug; those requests require a Jira ticket and a 2FA-approved access window.
- Backups & snapshots: backups are incremental, encrypted, and retained per the snapshot TTL. For Dedicated customers we can shorten the default TTL to 14 days or export snapshots to customer-owned buckets on request.
- Training pipeline block: there is an automated tag applied to all records originating in diagnostics that prevents them from entering training ingestion. The tag is enforced by the dataset-building job (read-only allowlist).

I'll attach the telemetry retention matrix (attached) and can provision the Config-as-Code snippet that lets Acme set telemetry=false at the tenant level.

Grace O'Connor
Sr. Platform Engineer, Redwood Inference
